title: Grateful Dead Live at Capital Centre on 1982-09-15
lineage: Cassette Master (Nakamichi DR-1/Dolby B) -> Sound Devices 744T (24bit/96k) ->Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: High‑quality soundboard capture of a jam‑heavy 1982 show with standout Shakedown, Saint, Not Fade Away and Stella Blue performances.
ai_review.review: The recording, taken from Healy’s AKG mics fed directly from the board, delivers a clear analog picture with only occasional crunchiness. Musically the concert is driven by nonstop "Playin'" jams, a killer Shakedown opener, a blistering Saint and sweet renditions of Not Fade Away and Stella Blue, though some listeners note low volume and an over‑prominent Bob slide.

ai_rating.rationale: Both reviewers gave five stars and praised the performance; recording is generally good with minor technical quirks, yielding a strong combined rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Recorded from Healy's AKG mics at the board – crisp analog sound with occasional crunch on louder sections (e.g., Saint, NFA). One reviewer mentions some recording issues but overall considers it a top‑tier audience‑style capture for the era.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is woven together by recurring "Playin'" jam themes, moving from Playin' → Crazy Fingers → Playin', through Red Rooster and Roses into Let It Grow, then a powerful second‑set opening with Shakedown that segues back into Playin' before launching into Sailor, Saint, NFA and Stella Blue.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Second reviewer felt Jerry made little impression; no specific praise or criticism beyond general performance notes.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob's slide work was called out as excessive, and he took a bathroom break during Red Rooster; otherwise his playing is appreciated.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland’s keyboards were highlighted as adding an "auditory assault" on Red Rooster.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both reviewers praised the drummers, with one noting this was the only time seeing "The Beast" and lauding the drum‑and‑space sections.
